problem: Existing social-navigation datasets are either small with inconsistent reasoning-action alignment (SNEI, 810 conversations), lack language/action supervision (SCAND, MuSoHu), or are VQA-style diagnostics without action labels (SocialNav-SUB, 600 samples). No large-scale egocentric dataset supports fine-tuning VLMs for short-horizon socially compliant decisions.
motivation: Socially compliant navigation needs structured reasoning about dynamic pedestrians and static constraints, and untuned VLMs do not reliably understand fine-grained social norms. Small VLMs are needed for real-time deployment but require high-quality, consistent CoT plus action supervision to learn this.
key_idea: Build MUSON, a 10,110-sample egocentric dataset from MuSoHu with human-verified five-step CoT annotations (perception, prediction, reasoning, action, explanation) and a standardized six-action space, and use it to fine-tune and benchmark small VLMs.
insight: Consistent CoT annotation quality matters more than the presence of CoT: with Qwen3-VL-2B, adding CoT improves MUSON accuracy from 0.5499 to 0.6899 but lowers SNEI accuracy from 0.6235 to 0.5741, attributed to SNEI's inconsistent reasoning/action/explanation. Per-action accuracy and Macro-F1 show that turn actions (rare classes) are near zero for most non-Qwen models even when overall accuracy looks acceptable.
method: Data collection: 10,110 single-frame egocentric samples curated from MuSoHu across 8 indoor/outdoor scene types (street, mall, shopping street, campus, park, supermarket, plaza, library), sparse to dense crowds, with a strictly ego-centric relative-direction frame.

Six-action space: Move Forward (54.48%), Move Forward Right (22.75%), Move Forward Left (15.47%), Stop (5.49%), Turn Right (1.06%), Turn Left (0.75%); keeps forward priors while retaining safety-critical corner cases.
Five-step CoT schema: perception, prediction, reasoning, action, explanation, linking visual evidence, predicted pedestrian motion, social norms and physical constraints to the final action.

Annotation pipeline: GPT-5.4-mini generates initial annotations, nine human experts verify/revise and determine the final action, then a consistency check re-examines ambiguous or inconsistent samples.
Four evaluation tasks: social action planning, social-context scene perception, socially-aligned CoT reasoning, and navigation explanation.

Metrics: accuracy, Macro-F1, per-action accuracy, manually judged collision rate (CR, a predicted action counts as a collision if it would hit pedestrians or obstacles), and SBERT cosine similarity for each CoT component.
Baseline SFT: full-parameter fine-tuning of LLM + connector with the vision tower frozen; a 'Safety Expert' system prompt enforces the five-step CoT format.

setting.backbone: Ten small VLMs (fine-tuned): TinyLLaVA (Phi-2), NVILA, InternVL3-1B/2B/8B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B, Qwen3-VL-2B/4B/8B
setting.training_data: MUSON train split of 8,088 samples (8:2 split), 10 epochs, AdamW lr 2e-5, cosine schedule, global batch 32, 8x A100, 448x448 images
setting.action_space: six discrete high-level semantic actions (Move Forward, Forward Left, Forward Right, Stop, Turn Left, Turn Right)
setting.simulator: none (offline evaluation on real-world MuSoHu-derived frames)

numbers.extra: 5-step CoT SFT on MUSON train (8,088 samples)

numbers_note: MUSON is a new benchmark, so all numbers are on its own test split; the SNEI ablation (Action Only 0.6235, With CoT 0.5741) is on a different dataset and is not listed above.
results: Fine-tuned on MUSON, Qwen3-VL-8B is best on decision quality (Acc 0.7765, Macro-F1 0.7490, CR 0.0609), ahead of Qwen2.5-VL-7B (0.7520 / 0.6695 / 0.0645). Qwen-series models handle turn actions far better, while InternVL3, TinyLLaVA and NVILA score near zero on Turn Left/Right. CoT supervision lifts Qwen3-VL-2B accuracy from 0.5499 to 0.6899 on MUSON.
limitations: Single-frame, short-horizon, discrete six-action setting with no closed-loop or real-robot evaluation, and action labels are subjective.
Severe long-tail class imbalance (Turn Left 0.75%, Turn Right 1.06%) leaves rare-action performance weak and noisy.

Collision rate is judged manually, and annotations are partly generated by GPT-5.4-mini; SBERT similarity is only a proxy for reasoning quality. All models are evaluated only after fine-tuning, with no untuned or large-VLM baseline in the tables.
